question.:question/problem:
Find the general solution to the differential equation ${y}^{′}=\frac{x}{y},$ given that $K$ is an arbitrary constant.

$y=\pm ($ {{field-1}} $+K)^{1/2}$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we separate the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{x}{y} \\ y\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int y\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int x\,\text{d}x \\ \int y\,\text{d}y & =\int x\,\text{d}x \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{2} & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $y.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}^{2}}{2} & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+C \\ {y}^{2} & ={x}^{2}+2C \\ {y}^{2} & ={x}^{2}+K \\ y & =\pm \sqrt{{x}^{2}+K} \\ y & =\pm ({x}^{2}+K)^{1/2},\end{aligned}
$$

where $K=2C$ is an arbitrary constant.
